def-emg-fx-linearized-electrovac:
## Definition

Assume the countable-choice background $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ carried by the stated Lorentzian geometry suppliers. Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be an oriented, time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, with metric-selected connection and orientation as in the geometric electrovac convention. In a length-coordinate chart, metric components are dimensionless and a geometric-normalized real two-form has components of unit $\mathrm{m}^{-1}$.

For a smooth real two-form $\mathcal F$, put
$$Q_{ab}(g,\mathcal F):=\mathcal F_{ac}\mathcal F_b{}^c-\frac14 g_{ab}\mathcal F_{cd}\mathcal F^{cd},$$
where all raised indices use $g^{-1}$. Its length-coordinate components have unit $\mathrm{m}^{-2}$. Fix $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ with unit $\mathrm{m}^{-2}$. An **exact geometric electrovacuum background on $U\subseteq M$** is a smooth pair $(g,\mathcal F)$ on the same open set satisfying
$$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}[g]-\Lambda g_{ab}=2Q_{ab}(g,\mathcal F),\qquad d\mathcal F=0,\qquad d(\star_g\mathcal F)=0.$$
For $\Lambda=0$ this is the geometric normalization of [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]]. The symbol $\mathcal F$ here is geometric-normalized; it is not the SI-normalized field tensor used in [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]].

Fix such a background on $U$. A **linearized perturbation** is a pair $(h,f)$ consisting of a smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor $h$ and a smooth real two-form $f$ on $U$. Its linearized metric residual is
$$\delta E_{(g,\mathcal F)}[h,f]:=\left.\frac{d}{d\epsilon}\right|_{\epsilon=0}\bigl(\operatorname{Ric}[g_\epsilon]-\Lambda g_\epsilon-2Q(g_\epsilon,\mathcal F_\epsilon)\bigr),$$
and its linearized Maxwell residuals are
$$df,\qquad d\,\delta(\star\mathcal F),\qquad \delta(\star\mathcal F):=\left.\frac{d}{d\epsilon}\right|_{\epsilon=0}\star_{g_\epsilon}\mathcal F_\epsilon.$$
Here $g_\epsilon=g+\epsilon h+O(\epsilon^2)$ and $\mathcal F_\epsilon=\mathcal F+\epsilon f+O(\epsilon^2)$ are smooth local families on the fixed domain, with dimensionless parameter $\epsilon$. The derivatives are the coordinatewise derivatives of these smooth finite-jet operators; the chain rule makes them depend only on $(h,f)$, not on the higher-order parts of the chosen families. The **linearized electrovacuum system** is the homogeneous system $\delta E_{(g,\mathcal F)}[h,f]=0$, $df=0$, and $d\,\delta(\star\mathcal F)=0$.

For a smooth vector field $X$, let $\Phi_\epsilon$ be its local flow and define the **pure gauge perturbation** by $(h,f)=\left.\frac{d}{d\epsilon}\right|_0(\Phi_\epsilon^*g,\Phi_\epsilon^*\mathcal F)$. A **parameter perturbation** is the derivative of a smooth one-parameter family of exact geometric electrovacuum backgrounds on one common open domain. Neither definition asserts that every solution of the linearized system is pure gauge or is a parameter perturbation.

For a local diffeomorphism $\Phi:V\to W$ and a covariant $r$-tensor $T$ on $W$, its pullback is $(\Phi^*T)_p(v_1,\ldots,v_r):=T_{\Phi(p)}(D\Phi_pv_1,\ldots,D\Phi_pv_r)$; this fixes the pullback convention in the pure-gauge definition.

If a potential perturbation $a\in\Omega^1(V)$ is chosen on an open set $V\subseteq U$ with $f=da$, then $a$ and $a+d\chi$ represent the same field-strength perturbation for every smooth scalar $\chi$ on $V$. No global exactness of $f$ or global potential is assumed.
lem-emg-fx-linearized-hodge:
## Statement

Let $g_\epsilon=g+\epsilon h+O(\epsilon^2)$ be a smooth variation of an oriented Lorentzian metric on a four-manifold, and let $\omega_\epsilon=\omega+\epsilon\tau+O(\epsilon^2)$ be a smooth variation of a $k$-form, $0\le k\le4$. Define $h_a{}^b:=g^{bc}h_{ac}$, $\operatorname{tr}_g h:=g^{ab}h_{ab}$, and
$$\bigl(h^\sharp\!\cdot\omega\bigr)_{a_1\ldots a_k}:=\sum_{j=1}^k h_{a_j}{}^b\omega_{a_1\ldots a_{j-1}b a_{j+1}\ldots a_k},$$
with $h^\sharp\!\cdot\omega:=0$ for $k=0$. Then
$$\left.\frac{d}{d\epsilon}\right|_0\star_{g_\epsilon}\omega_\epsilon=\star_g\left(\tau+\frac12(\operatorname{tr}_g h)\omega-h^\sharp\!\cdot\omega\right).$$
In particular, for the geometric background $\mathcal F$ and perturbation $f$ of [[def-emg-fx-linearized-electrovac]],
$$\delta(\star\mathcal F)=\star_g\left(f+\frac12(\operatorname{tr}_g h)\mathcal F-h^\sharp\!\cdot\mathcal F\right).$$
If $(h,f)$ satisfies the linearized Maxwell equation, then $d\,\delta(\star\mathcal F)=0$; this last condition is exactly the derivative of $d(\star_{g_\epsilon}\mathcal F_\epsilon)=0$, not a consequence of the variation formula alone.
prop-emg-fx-gauge-linearized-solutions:
## Statement

Let $(g,\mathcal F)$ be a smooth exact geometric electrovacuum background on an open domain $U$ as in [[def-emg-fx-linearized-electrovac]]. If $X$ is a smooth vector field with local flow $\Phi_\epsilon$, then the pure-gauge perturbation $(\dot\Phi_0^*g,\dot\Phi_0^*\mathcal F)$ solves the linearized electrovacuum system on every common flow domain. More generally, the derivative at any parameter value of a smooth one-parameter family of exact backgrounds on a common domain solves the same linearized system. In particular, the fixed-domain Reissner–Nordström and Kerr–Newman parameter families provide such stationary parameter modes on their stated exterior domains. These conclusions classify neither the kernel of the linearized operator nor its integrable elements.
lem-emg-fx-local-linear-wave-control:
## Statement

Let $T>0$ and consider a smooth exact geometric electrovacuum background on a normal-flow collar $[-T,T]\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, where $x^0=t$ is a length coordinate, $n=\partial_t$, and
$$g=-dt^2+\gamma_{ij}(t,\theta)d\theta^i d\theta^j$$
with $\gamma$ a smooth positive spatial metric. Fix the harmonic reference metric $\bar g$ to equal the background and define $H^a[g_\epsilon]:=g_\epsilon^{bc}(\Gamma^a{}_{bc}[g_\epsilon]-\bar\Gamma^a{}_{bc})$, with $H_b[g_\epsilon]:=g_{\epsilon bc}H^c[g_\epsilon]$. Thus the background gauge vector vanishes and the linearized reduced metric equation is the derivative of $\operatorname{Ric}[g_\epsilon]-\nabla^{g_\epsilon}_{(a}H_{b)}[g_\epsilon]-\Lambda g_{\epsilon ab}-2Q_{ab}(g_\epsilon,\mathcal F_\epsilon)=0$, where $Q_{ab}(g,\mathcal F)=\mathcal F_{ac}\mathcal F_b{}^c-\tfrac14g_{ab}\mathcal F_{cd}\mathcal F^{cd}$. Let $L_0>0$ be the fixed spatial length scale and write $X^i=L_0\theta^i$ with dimensionless coordinates $\theta^i$ on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$. Use the global coordinate frame on $\mathbb T^3$ and the smooth oriented spatial orthonormal triad obtained by Gram–Schmidt from it. The first-order state is the $56$-component periodic array $u=(h_{ab},p_{ab},q_{abi},e_i,b_i)$, where $h$ is the metric perturbation, $p_{ab}=\bar\nabla_0h_{ab}$, $q_{abi}=\bar\nabla_i h_{ab}$, and $e_i,b_i$ are the six components of the two-form perturbation $f$ in the background triad. For arrays on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, define $H^k$ by the Fourier norm $\|u\|_{H^k}^2=\sum_{\ell\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+|\ell|^2)^k|\widehat u(\ell)|^2$. Write $x=\theta$ in the system below and absorb the fixed factor $L_0^{-1}$ from $\partial_{X^i}=L_0^{-1}\partial_{\theta^i}$ into its spatial matrices. For any smooth linearized perturbation state $u$ and smooth source $s$, write the inhomogeneous first-order system in the chosen trivialization as
$$A^0(t,x)\partial_tu+\sum_{i=1}^3 A^i(t,x)\partial_i u+C(t,x)u=s(t,x),$$
where $A^0,A^1,A^2,A^3,C$ are smooth periodic matrices, each $A^i$ and $A^0$ is symmetric, and constants $0<a\le b<\infty$ satisfy $aI\le A^0(t,x)\le bI$ throughout the slab. In the normal-flow chart, the harmonic metric reduction has time matrix $\operatorname{diag}(I,I,\gamma^{ij}I)$ and symmetric spatial matrices by [F1], while the six Maxwell field-strength variables have time matrix $I_6$ and symmetric spatial matrices by [F2]. When the Maxwell equations are linearized, derivatives of the perturbed lapse, frame and spatial metric occur through $p_{ab}$ and $q_{abi}$, which are components of the state and hence contribute to $C u$, not to spatial derivatives of the state. The variation of the Maxwell stress in the metric equation is algebraic in $(h,f)$ by [F3]. Thus the full principal matrices are the direct sums of the metric and Maxwell principal matrices, and the remaining couplings are smooth zeroth-order terms. Compactness of the slab then supplies uniform positive bounds for $A^0$.

For every integer $k\ge0$, define
$$\mathcal E_k(t):=\sum_{|\alpha|\le k}\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}(\partial^\alpha u)^T A^0(t,x)\partial^\alpha u\,dx.$$
There is a constant $C_k$, depending only on $a,b,T$ and the coefficient derivatives through order $k+1$, such that
$$\|u(t)\|_{H^k}\le C_k e^{C_k|t|}\left(\|u(0)\|_{H^k}+\int_{\min(0,t)}^{\max(0,t)}\|s(\tau)\|_{H^k}\,d\tau\right),\qquad |t|\le T.$$
This is a finite-time conditional estimate, not an existence theorem or a global decay statement.

For the unforced linearized system, the Maxwell subsidiary constraints are the spatial restrictions of $df$ and $d\,\delta(\star\mathcal F)$ to a slice. If the normal-slot linearized Maxwell evolution equations hold and both initial restrictions vanish, they remain zero on the slab. Let $\dot H$ be the first variation of the harmonic gauge vector at the exact background. If the linearized reduced Einstein and Maxwell equations hold and $\dot H=\partial_t\dot H=0$ initially, then $\dot H=0$ throughout the slab. These are the Maxwell Gauss and harmonic-gauge subsidiary identities; no decay of the physical perturbation is asserted.
